attacks.claim: The retry uses a fixed delay with no jitter and no retry budget. When the upstream is saturated, all throttled requests retry at the same moment, which is a synchronized retry storm that adds load exactly when the upstream is least able to handle it. Requests also hold open for up to 5s without honoring client abort during the sleep.
attacks.evidence: const delay = retryAfterMs(...); await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, delay));  // no jitter, no budget, no signal check

attacks.claim: Upstream 429s are retried in-request with no concurrency cap. Each retry holds the client connection and a socket for up to 5s plus the second upstream round trip, so a sustained upstream 429 storm (for example the 400 rps batch scenario in the description) multiplies held connections and upstream calls. A Retry-After of 0 causes an immediate retry, which adds load to an already-saturated upstream.

attacks.claim: The spec says any other upstream error is passed straight through, but upstream.chat is not wrapped. A network or timeout exception will propagate as an unhandled error (typically a 500) rather than being forwarded as the upstream error. No error-path tests exist.
